docs.title: vexy-dexyjs
docs.text:
vexy-dexyjs turns a web page into slides, in the browser.

It is a small, dependency-free DOM preprocessor. You run it inside a page that is already loaded. It rewrites that page into a flat list of <section class="slide"> elements and tags each one with a shared set of layout classes. A slide renderer such as reveal.js, or CSS paged media, can then take the result and print it to PDF.

Because it runs where the page already lives, fonts, stylesheets and images stay loaded. Nothing is downloaded and rewired offline.

vexy-dexyjs is the generalized successor to webflow2revealjs. Instead of assuming Webflow markup, it accepts a framework hint for Webflow, Framer, MkDocs Material, Docusaurus, Bubble or plain HTML (generic).

docs.title: What goes in, what comes out
Where to go next
docs.text:
• Installation: npm, CDN script tag, or build from source.
  • Quick start: convert a page from the browser console or from a headless browser.
  • How it works: the four stages of preprocess(), followed through one example page.
  • Frameworks: what each framework value removes and where it reads slides from.
  • API reference: every exported function and its exact behaviour.
  • Chrome extension: the Manifest V3 scaffold under extension/.
  • Troubleshooting: known limits and how to work around them.
  • Development: build, test and release.

docs.title: Consumers
docs.text:
• vexy-dexypy is the Python command-line tool that drives a headless browser, injects this bundle, and renders the slides to PDF. npm run build writes the bundle it vendors.
  • The Chrome extension scaffold injects the global bundle into the active tab.
  • Any other tool can import the module or load the global bundle with a <script> tag.

docs.title: License
docs.text: See the LICENSE file in the repository.

docs.title: API reference
docs.text:
All functions are named exports of the module and properties of window.VexyDexy in the global bundle. Types are declared in index.d.ts.

import {
  preprocess,
  parseCssBackgroundColors,
  luminance,
  getBgClass,
  getSectionBgColor,
  wrapContentsInDiv,
  normalizeSlideDom,
  isChromeElement,
  ensureSectionTag,
} from "vexy-dexyjs";

The first function does the whole job. The others are the steps it is built from, exported for testing and for tools that want to run only part of the pipeline.

docs.title: preprocess
docs.text:
function preprocess(config?: PreprocessConfig): PreprocessResult;

Rewrites the global document in place into slide sections and returns the serialized result. Needs a rendered DOM. See How it works for the full pipeline.

config is optional. Its fields:

Field Type Default Effect framework string "generic" Selects chrome removal and slide rules. One of generic, webflow, framer, mkdocs-material, docusaurus, bubble; other strings act like generic. See Frameworks. stageWidth number 1920 Accepted and defaulted, but not used by the current code. stageHeight number 1080 Accepted and defaulted, but not used by the current code. breaks { y: number }[] [] Vertical offsets in CSS pixels from the top of the document. Used only by the block split. Each break starts a new slide at the closest content block within 200 px.

Returns { html: string }, where html is document.documentElement.outerHTML after the rewrite.

docs.title: parseCssBackgroundColors
docs.text:
function parseCssBackgroundColors(cssContent: string): Record<string, string>;

Scans raw CSS text and returns a map from class name to background colour. Does not need a DOM.

  • Comments are stripped first.
  • The text is walked by brace depth, so rules inside @media and other nested blocks are read too.
  • A background-color value is read up to the first space, ; or !, so rgb(0, 0, 0) is recorded as rgb(0, (see Troubleshooting). A background shorthand is used only when its value starts with # or rgb, or is one of red, blue, green, white, black or transparent.
  • The colour is stored for the last class in each comma-separated selector, so .card .title { … } records title.
  • When the same class appears more than once, the selector with the higher specificity wins: one point per ., ten per #. On a tie, the later rule wins.
parseCssBackgroundColors(`
  .a { background-color: #111111; }
  #id.a { background-color: #222222; }
  @media (min-width: 600px) { .b { background: #fff; } }
`);
// → { a: "#222222", b: "#fff" }

docs.title: luminance
docs.text:
function luminance(color: string): number;

Returns the brightness of a CSS colour from 0 (black) to 1 (white), computed as 0.2126·R + 0.7152·G + 0.0722·B on channel values scaled to 0–1.

Accepted formats are #rgb, #rrggbb, rgb(r, g, b) and rgba(r, g, b, a) (alpha is ignored). Anything else, including named colours, #rgba, #rrggbbaa, an empty string and null, returns 1, as if the colour were white.

luminance("#1a1a2e"); // ≈ 0.108
luminance("navy");    // 1 (named colours are not parsed)

docs.title: getBgClass
docs.text:
function getBgClass(color: string | null | undefined): string;

Returns "slide-dark-bg" when luminance(color) is below 0.5, otherwise "slide-light-bg". Missing colours and the values transparent, rgba(0, 0, 0, 0), rgba(0,0,0,0), initial and inherit return "slide-light-bg".

docs.title: getSectionBgColor
docs.text:
function getSectionBgColor(
  classes: string[],
  classColors: Record<string, string>,
): string | null;

Walks classes from last to first and returns the colour of the first class found in classColors, or null. Later classes win, as they usually do in the browser.

getSectionBgColor(["a", "b"], { a: "#112233", b: "#445566" }); // "#445566"

docs.title: normalizeSlideDom
docs.text:
function normalizeSlideDom(sec: Element, classColors: Record<string, string>): void;

Adds the slide layout classes to one section element, in place: slide, a background class and data-background-color, then slide-badge, slide-split-layout, slide-column, slide-text-container, slide-image-container and slide-image-cover as the section's shape requires. The rules are listed in How it works.

docs.title: wrapContentsInDiv
docs.text:
function wrapContentsInDiv(parent: Element, wrapperClass: string): void;

Moves the child nodes of parent into a new <div class="wrapperClass"> appended to parent. <script> and <style> children, and element children whose class names contain mask, video-wrap or hover-video, are not wrapped; they are moved after the new wrapper. This gives text one container to style while background media stays where CSS expects it.

Uses the global Node, so it needs a browser-like environment.

docs.title: isChromeElement
docs.text:
function isChromeElement(el: Element): boolean;

Returns true when the element looks like page chrome: its class names or id contain, or its tag name equals, one of menu, nav, footer, header, banner, sidebar or search.

The check is a substring match, so a class such as navigation-cards or researcher also counts as chrome.

docs.title: ensureSectionTag
docs.text:
function ensureSectionTag(el: Element): Element;

Returns el if it is a <section>. Otherwise creates a new <section>, copies all of el's attributes onto it, moves el's children into it and returns it. The new section is not inserted into the document; el is left empty.

docs.title: Types
docs.text:
interface Break { y: number }

type Framework =
  | "generic" | "webflow" | "framer"
  | "mkdocs-material" | "docusaurus" | "bubble";

interface PreprocessConfig {
  framework?: Framework | string;
  stageWidth?: number;
  stageHeight?: number;
  breaks?: Break[];
}

interface PreprocessResult { html: string }

index.d.ts also declares window.VexyDexy with all nine functions.

docs.title: Development
docs.text: This page covers the repository layout, the build, the tests, the documentation site and the release process.

docs.title: Repository layout
docs.text: Path Contents src/index.js The whole library: nine exported functions. index.d.ts Hand-maintained type declarations that mirror src/index.js. test/unit.test.js vitest unit tests for the DOM-free helpers, run against src/. test/smoke.mjs Smoke test that imports the built dist/index.mjs. extension/ Manifest V3 Chrome extension scaffold. See Chrome extension. src_docs/md/ Source of this documentation. src_docs/mkdocs.yml Documentation site configuration. docs/ The built documentation site, served by GitHub Pages. Generated; do not edit.

docs.title: Build the bundles
docs.text:
Prerequisites: Node.js and npm.

  1. Install the development dependencies:

    npm ci

  2. Run the build:

    npm run build

npm run build runs six esbuild scripts in sequence:

Script Output Format build:esm dist/index.mjs ES module build:cjs dist/index.cjs CommonJS build:iife dist/vexy-dexyjs.global.js IIFE, global VexyDexy build:cdn dist/vexy-dexyjs.global.min.js IIFE, minified build:py ../vexy-dexypy/src/vexy_dexypy/assets/vexy-dexyjs.js IIFE, minified build:ext extension/vexy-dexyjs.global.min.js IIFE, minified

build:py writes into a sibling checkout of vexy-dexypy, which vendors the bundle. Keep the two repositories side by side, or run the other scripts individually.

The root build.sh wraps both builds:

./build.sh            # documentation and bundles
./build.sh docs       # documentation only
./build.sh package    # npm run build only

docs.title: Run the tests
docs.text:
npm run test:unit     # vitest, against src/, no build needed
npm test              # smoke test, needs dist/index.mjs from npm run build

The unit tests cover luminance, getBgClass, parseCssBackgroundColors and getSectionBgColor. The smoke test checks that all nine exports are functions and repeats a few helper checks against the built bundle.

preprocess() itself needs a browser DOM, so these tests do not exercise it. The repository's TODO.md plans DOM-backed tests with saved fixture pages.

docs.title: Continuous integration
docs.text: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs on every push and pull request to main. On Node 18, 20 and 22 it runs npm ci, npm run build, npm run test:unit and npm test.

docs.title: Build the documentation
docs.text:
The site is built with ProperDocs and the MaterialX theme. You need uv; uvx downloads the pinned tools on first use.

src_docs/build.sh          # strict build of src_docs/md/ into docs/
src_docs/build.sh serve    # live preview on http://127.0.0.1:8000

.github/workflows/docs.yml runs the same build on every push to main that changes src_docs/ and commits the result to docs/. GitHub Pages serves docs/ at https://vexy.dev/vexy-dexyjs/.

Edit pages in src_docs/md/, never in docs/: the build replaces docs/ completely.

docs.title: Release
docs.text:
The version comes from git tags (vX.Y.Z).

./publish.sh releases from your machine. It:

  1. stages all changes with git add .,
  2. runs uvx gitnextver, which commits and creates the next semver tag,
  3. pushes main and the tags to origin,
  4. sets the package.json version to the latest tag without the v,
  5. runs npm run build, and
  6. runs npm publish --access public.

.github/workflows/npm-publish.yml also publishes. It runs when a tag matching v* is pushed: it builds, runs both test suites, and runs npm publish --provenance --access public with the NPM_TOKEN secret.

Warning

publish.sh pushes a tag, which starts the workflow, and also publishes locally. Only one of the two npm publish calls can succeed for a given version. The tagged commit also still carries the previous package.json version, because step 4 runs after the tag is created.

docs.title: Coding notes
docs.text:
• Source files start with a this_file comment that holds their path.
  • src/index.js has no runtime dependencies. Keep it that way: the bundle is injected into arbitrary pages.
  • When you change an exported signature, update index.d.ts and the window.VexyDexy declaration in it.

docs.title: Chrome extension
docs.text: The extension/ folder holds a minimal Manifest V3 extension. It runs preprocess() against the active tab and rewrites that page into slides in place. It is a starting point, not a finished product.

docs.title: What it contains
docs.text: File Purpose manifest.json Manifest V3. Requests the activeTab and scripting permissions and opens popup.html from the toolbar button. popup.html A framework selector (generic, webflow, framer, mkdocs-material, docusaurus, bubble) and a Convert to slides button. popup.js Injects the bundle into the active tab with chrome.scripting.executeScript, then calls preprocess() there. vexy-dexyjs.global.min.js The minified global bundle. Produced by npm run build:ext and ignored by git.

docs.title: Build and load the extension
docs.text:
Prerequisites: Google Chrome (or another Chromium browser that loads unpacked Manifest V3 extensions), Node.js and npm.

  1. In the repository root, install the dependencies:

    npm ci

  2. Build the bundle into the extension folder:

    npm run build:ext

    extension/vexy-dexyjs.global.min.js now exists. (npm run build also runs this step.)

  3. In Chrome, open chrome://extensions.

  4. Turn on Developer mode.
  5. Click Load unpacked and select the extension/ folder.

The extension appears as vexy-dexyjs — page to slides. Chrome lists new extensions under the puzzle-piece menu; pin it to keep the button in the toolbar. Its tooltip reads Convert page to slides.

docs.title: Convert a tab
docs.text:
1. Open the page you want to convert.
  2. Click the extension's toolbar button.
  3. Pick a framework from the list.
  4. Click Convert to slides.

The popup shows working…, then done — N chars (see page console), where N is the length of the serialized HTML. The page itself now shows only the slide sections. The page console logs [vexy-dexyjs] preprocessed HTML length: N.

If anything fails, the popup shows error: followed by the message. A common cause is a browser page that extensions may not script, such as chrome:// pages.

docs.title: What happens inside
docs.text:
popup.js runs two scripts in the tab:

  1. files: ["vexy-dexyjs.global.min.js"] loads the bundle, which defines window.VexyDexy.
  2. A function that calls window.VexyDexy.preprocess({ framework }), logs the HTML length, and returns { length } to the popup.

Both run in the extension's isolated world for that tab, so the page's own Content Security Policy does not block the injection.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• The page is changed in place. Reload it to get the original back.
  • The extension does not save the HTML, open it in reveal.js, or print it. Those steps happen downstream of preprocess() and are left out on purpose.
  • manifest.json declares no icons, so Chrome shows a default one.

docs.title: Frameworks
docs.text:
The framework option tells preprocess() which page chrome to remove and where the slide content lives. generic is the default and works on any page.

VexyDexy.preprocess({ framework: "mkdocs-material" });

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
framework Removed before slicing Content root Slides from generic chrome children of the content root <body> block split at h1/h2 or breaks webflow .w-webflow-badge <body> top-level sections, else section blocks framer nothing extra <body> top-level sections, else [data-framer-name] mkdocs-material .md-sidebar, .md-header, .md-footer, .md-search, .md-nav, .md-source-file, .md-content__button, header, nav, footer article.md-content__inner block split docusaurus .navbar, .theme-doc-sidebar-container, footer, nav .theme-doc-markdown block split bubble none; inline position: absolute becomes relative <body> block split

"Block split" and "top-level sections" are described in How it works. Whichever path builds the slides, every slide then goes through the same normalization, so the output classes are the same for all frameworks.

If the content root selector matches nothing, <body> is used instead. Any framework string not in the table behaves like generic.

docs.title: generic
docs.text:
Use it for hand-written HTML, blogs and any site not listed below.

No framework-specific elements are removed up front. During the block split, direct children of <body> that look like chrome (see isChromeElement()) are removed, then the page is split before every h1 and h2, or at the positions given in breaks.

docs.title: webflow
docs.text:
1. Removes every .w-webflow-badge element.
  2. Takes the direct children of <body> that carry content and are not chrome. Webflow sections are often div elements such as <div class="hero"> rather than <section> tags, so this matches them where a section selector would not.
  3. If fewer than two qualify (for example, when everything sits inside one .page-wrapper), uses section, .section and [data-framer-name] elements anywhere in the body.
  4. If that also yields fewer than two, falls back to the block split.

docs.title: framer
docs.text: Same as webflow, without the badge removal. Framer layers carry a data-framer-name attribute, which the second step picks up.

docs.title: mkdocs-material
docs.text: Removes the Material for MkDocs header, navigation, sidebars, search, footer, the "edit this page" buttons and the source-file footer, then splits the article (article.md-content__inner) at its h1 and h2 headings. Each second-level section of the documentation page becomes one slide.

docs.title: docusaurus
docs.text: Removes the navbar, the docs sidebar, footer and nav elements, then splits .theme-doc-markdown at its headings.

docs.title: bubble
docs.text: Bubble pages position most elements absolutely. The preprocessor sets every element whose inline style is position: absolute to position: relative, so the elements flow vertically, then applies the block split to <body>.

docs.title: Choosing a value
docs.text:
• The site was built with one of the listed tools: use that value.
  • Webflow or Framer produced fewer slides than expected: the page probably nests its sections. Try generic, which splits by headings, or pass breaks.
  • Anything else: use generic.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text: preprocess() runs four stages against the live document. This page explains each stage and then follows one small page through all of them.

docs.title: Stage 1: collect background colours
docs.text:
Slides need to know whether they are light or dark. The preprocessor builds a map from CSS class name to background colour in two passes.

  1. Live stylesheets. It walks document.styleSheets and their cssRules. For every rule with a background-color (or a background value) that is not transparent, rgba(0, 0, 0, 0), initial or inherit, it records the colour for every class in the selector. Stylesheets that throw on access, such as cross-origin sheets, are skipped silently.
  2. Inline <style> elements. It parses the text of every <style> element with parseCssBackgroundColors() and merges the result over the first map, so these values win.

docs.title: Stage 2: select or build slides
docs.text:
First the preprocessor removes framework chrome and picks a content root. Both depend on the framework value; Frameworks lists them.

Then it decides what a slide is.

docs.title: Webflow and Framer: top-level sections
docs.text:
For webflow and framer, it takes the direct children of the content root that:

  • are not script, style, noscript, iframe or link elements,
  • are not page chrome according to isChromeElement(),
  • are not the .w-webflow-badge, and
  • contain text, or an img, svg, video or picture element.

If at least two remain, each one becomes a slide. If not, it looks for section, .section and [data-framer-name] elements anywhere in the content root and uses those if there are at least two. If that also fails, it uses the block split below.

docs.title: Every other case: block split
docs.text:
1. Direct children of the content root that look like chrome are removed (except <section> elements).
  2. The content root is walked recursively to collect content blocks:
    • headings h1–h6, p, pre, table, ul, ol, img, blockquote;
    • any element with an inline position: absolute, position: relative or background-color, or whose style attribute mentions position or background;
    • div, section, article, main, aside, form, body, header and footer elements that have no block-level children of their own.
  3. Blocks that are hidden (display: none) or have zero height are dropped. The rest are sorted by their vertical position in the document.
  4. Split points are chosen:
    • For each entry in breaks, the block whose top edge is closest to y becomes a split point, if it is less than 200 px away.
    • If no break matched, or breaks is empty, every h1 and h2 after the first block becomes a split point.
  5. The blocks are cloned, in order, into new <section> elements, starting a new section at each split point.

docs.title: Stage 3: normalize each slide
docs.text:
Each slide element is converted to a <section> with ensureSectionTag() and passed to normalizeSlideDom(), which adds layout classes:

  1. Background. The section gets the class slide. Its colour comes from the colour map (later classes win), else its inline background-color, else an existing data-background-color attribute. A colour found this way is written to data-background-color, and the section gets slide-light-bg or slide-dark-bg according to getBgClass(). Without a colour, the section gets slide-light-bg.
  2. Badge or card. If exactly one descendant div has card or badge in its class names, it gets slide-badge. If several do, and exactly one of them also has kapr- in its class names, that one is chosen. Every image in the section then gets slide-image-cover, its parent gets slide-image-container, and normalization stops.
  3. Columns. The preprocessor lists the direct div and section children, ignoring those whose class names contain menu, nav, footer, mask, header or banner. If there is exactly one and its class names contain grid, container, row, wrap or bleed, it looks one level deeper, at that wrapper's div and section children (ignoring mask, video-wrap and hover-video).
    • Two columns: the wrapper (or the section) gets slide-split-layout and each column gets slide-column. A column whose class carries a background colour gets it as an inline background-color: … !important. A column with an image gets slide-image-container and its first image gets slide-image-cover. A column without an image gets a slide-text-container: either its only div child, when that child's class names contain text or head, or a new div wrapped around its content.
    • More than two columns: each column whose class carries a background colour gets that colour as an inline background-color: … !important. No layout classes are added.
  4. Single block. With zero or one column, a section that has an image but no h1, h2, h3 or p is treated as a picture: the image gets slide-image-cover and its parent slide-image-container. Otherwise the first descendant div whose class names contain hero-wrap, container or front becomes the slide-text-container. If there is none, the section's content is wrapped in a new div.slide-text-container.

docs.title: Stage 4: replace the body
docs.text:
Every <link> and <style> element in the document is moved into <head>. document.body is then emptied and the normalized sections are appended to it. preprocess() returns { html: document.documentElement.outerHTML }.

Body content that did not end up in a slide is gone, including <script> elements in the body.

docs.title: Worked example
docs.text:
Take this page:

<html>
  <head>
    <style>
      .hero { background-color: #1a1a2e; }
      .features { background-color: #f5f5f5; }
    </style>
  </head>
  <body>
    <nav class="navbar"><a href="/">Home</a></nav>
    <div class="hero"><div class="hero-wrap"><h1>Fast fonts</h1><p>Intro.</p></div></div>
    <div class="features"><div class="grid">
      <div class="text-block"><h2>Variable</h2><p>One file.</p></div>
      <div class="image-block"><img src="a.png"></div>
    </div></div>
  </body>
</html>

and run preprocess({ framework: "webflow" }).

  1. Colours. The colour map is { hero: "#1a1a2e", features: "#f5f5f5" }.
  2. Slides. The body has three children. nav is chrome, so it is skipped. .hero and .features both contain text, which makes two top-level sections, so each becomes a slide.
  3. Normalize .hero. It is a div, so it is copied into a new <section>. #1a1a2e has a luminance of about 0.11, below 0.5, so the slide gets slide-dark-bg. Its only child, .hero-wrap, has no div children, so there are no columns. There is no image. .hero-wrap matches hero-wrap and becomes the slide-text-container.
  4. Normalize .features. #f5f5f5 is light. Its only child, .grid, matches grid, so the preprocessor looks at .grid's two children. Two columns means a split layout. .text-block has no image, so its content is wrapped in a new text container. .image-block has an image.
  5. Replace the body. The <nav> is gone and only the two sections remain.

Result (whitespace trimmed):

<body>
  <section class="hero slide slide-dark-bg" data-background-color="#1a1a2e">
    <div class="hero-wrap slide-text-container"><h1>Fast fonts</h1><p>Intro.</p></div>
  </section>
  <section class="features slide slide-light-bg" data-background-color="#f5f5f5">
    <div class="grid slide-split-layout">
      <div class="text-block slide-column">
        <div class="slide-text-container"><h2>Variable</h2><p>One file.</p></div>
      </div>
      <div class="image-block slide-column slide-image-container">
        <img src="a.png" class="slide-image-cover">
      </div>
    </div>
  </section>
</body>

docs.title: The layout vocabulary
docs.text:
These are the classes and attributes downstream renderers can style against.

Name Set on Meaning slide every slide <section> One slide. slide-light-bg slide <section> Background luminance is 0.5 or above, or unknown. slide-dark-bg slide <section> Background luminance is below 0.5. data-background-color slide <section> (attribute) The resolved background colour, as found in the CSS. slide-split-layout section or its grid wrapper Holds exactly two columns. slide-column each of the two columns One half of a split layout. slide-text-container a div The block that holds the slide's text. slide-image-container image parent or image column Holds a cover image. slide-image-cover img An image meant to fill its container. slide-badge a div The single card or badge in the slide.

vexy-dexyjs adds these classes but no CSS for them. Styling them is up to the renderer that consumes the output.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
vexy-dexyjs ships in four bundle formats. Pick the one that matches how you load JavaScript.

File Format Use it for dist/index.mjs ES module import in bundlers and modern browsers dist/index.cjs CommonJS require() dist/vexy-dexyjs.global.js IIFE, unminified <script> tags while debugging dist/vexy-dexyjs.global.min.js IIFE, minified <script> tags, CDN, content scripts

The IIFE bundles define one global, window.VexyDexy, which holds every exported function. Type declarations live in index.d.ts at the package root.

docs.title: From npm
docs.text:
npm install vexy-dexyjs

import { preprocess } from "vexy-dexyjs";

The package exports map resolves import to dist/index.mjs, require to dist/index.cjs, and types to index.d.ts.

Package not found?

If npm install vexy-dexyjs fails with a 404 error, the package has not been published to the npm registry yet. Build it from source instead (see below) and load the files from dist/.

docs.title: From a CDN
docs.text:
The unpkg and jsdelivr fields in package.json point at the minified global bundle, so a CDN serves it without a build step:

<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/vexy-dexyjs/dist/vexy-dexyjs.global.min.js"></script>
<script>
  const { html } = window.VexyDexy.preprocess({ framework: "generic" });
</script>

The CDN depends on the npm package, so the same note applies.

docs.title: From source
docs.text:
Prerequisites: Node.js and npm. CI tests on Node 18, 20 and 22.

  1. Clone the repository.

    git clone https://github.com/vexyart/vexy-dexyjs.git
cd vexy-dexyjs

  2. Install the development dependencies (esbuild and vitest).

    npm ci

  3. Build the bundles.

    npm run build

    The dist/ folder now contains the four files listed above.

npm run build writes outside the repository

The full build also runs build:py, which writes ../vexy-dexypy/src/vexy_dexypy/assets/vexy-dexyjs.js for the sibling vexy-dexypy checkout, and build:ext, which writes extension/vexy-dexyjs.global.min.js. To build only the npm bundles, run the individual scripts:

npm run build:esm && npm run build:cjs && npm run build:iife && npm run build:cdn

docs.title: Runtime requirements
docs.text:
preprocess() needs a real, rendered DOM. It reads document.styleSheets, calls getBoundingClientRect() and window.getComputedStyle(), and uses window.scrollY. Run it in:

  • a page script or the browser console,
  • an extension content script, or
  • a headless browser through page.evaluate().

The pure helpers (parseCssBackgroundColors, luminance, getBgClass, getSectionBgColor) do not touch the DOM and run in Node.js as well.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
This page converts one page to slides two ways: by hand in the browser, and automatically from a headless browser.

preprocess() rewrites the page it runs in. Reload the page to get the original back.

docs.title: Convert a page in the browser
docs.text:
Prerequisites: a desktop browser with developer tools, and the minified global bundle vexy-dexyjs.global.min.js, either from a CDN or from your own build (see Installation).

  1. Open the page you want to convert and wait until it has finished loading.
  2. Scroll to the bottom and back to the top, so that lazily loaded images and sections are in the DOM.
  3. Open the developer tools console.

  4. Load the bundle into the page:

    await new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
  const s = document.createElement("script");
  s.src = "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/vexy-dexyjs/dist/vexy-dexyjs.global.min.js";
  s.onload = resolve;
  s.onerror = reject;
  document.head.appendChild(s);
});

    window.VexyDexy is now defined. Pages with a strict Content Security Policy can block this step. Use the Chrome extension or a headless browser for those.

  5. Run the preprocessor with the framework hint that matches the site:

    const { html } = VexyDexy.preprocess({ framework: "generic" });
document.querySelectorAll("section.slide").length;

The page now shows only the slide sections, and the console prints how many there are. html holds the serialized document.

docs.title: Convert a page from a headless browser
docs.text:
vexy-dexypy works this way: it injects the bundle with Playwright for Python and calls window.VexyDexy.preprocess(config). The example uses Playwright for Node.js; any tool that can add a script to a page and evaluate a function in it works the same way.

Prerequisites: Node.js, Playwright (npm install playwright), and a local build of dist/vexy-dexyjs.global.min.js.

  1. Save this script as convert.mjs next to the dist/ folder:

    import { chromium } from "playwright";
import { writeFileSync } from "node:fs";

const browser = await chromium.launch();
const page = await browser.newPage({ viewport: { width: 1920, height: 1080 } });
await page.goto("https://example.com/", { waitUntil: "networkidle" });

// Inject the IIFE bundle; it defines window.VexyDexy in the page.
await page.addScriptTag({ path: "dist/vexy-dexyjs.global.min.js" });

// Run preprocess() inside the page and bring the HTML back to Node.
const html = await page.evaluate(
  (cfg) => window.VexyDexy.preprocess(cfg).html,
  { framework: "generic" },
);

writeFileSync("slides.html", html);
await browser.close();

  2. Run it:

    node convert.mjs

The script writes slides.html, the rewritten page with one <section class="slide"> per slide. <link> and <style> elements from the original page are kept in <head>, so the file still refers to the original stylesheets.

docs.title: Snap slides to known positions
docs.text:
On pages without framework sections, preprocess() splits the page before each h1 and h2. To choose the split points yourself, pass breaks: a list of vertical offsets in CSS pixels, measured from the top of the document.

VexyDexy.preprocess({
  framework: "generic",
  breaks: [{ y: 1080 }, { y: 2160 }],
});

For each break, the content block whose top edge is closest to y starts a new slide, provided it lies within 200 px. See How it works for the details.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Choose the right framework value in Frameworks.
  • Read the classes the output carries in How it works.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: This page lists known limits of the current code and what to do about them.

docs.title: The page turned into one slide
docs.text:
Cause. With the block split, slides start at h1 and h2 headings. A page that uses only h3 and smaller, or styled div elements as headings, has no split points.

Fix. Pass breaks with the vertical offsets where slides should start, or use the webflow or framer value if the page is built from top-level sections.

docs.title: Webflow or Framer produced the wrong slides
docs.text:
Cause. The top-level path takes every content-bearing direct child of <body>. On sites that wrap everything in one container it finds fewer than two, and falls back to section, .section and [data-framer-name] elements anywhere in the page, which may be nested at different depths.

Fix. Try generic, which splits by headings, and add breaks where needed.

docs.title: Content is missing from the output
docs.text:
Check these causes in order:

  1. Chrome detection. Top-level elements whose class names or id contain menu, nav, footer, header, banner, sidebar or search are treated as chrome and dropped: candidate sections for webflow and framer, and direct children of the content root for the block split. This is a substring match: class="research" contains search, and class="navigation-cards" contains nav.
  2. Hidden or empty blocks. The block split drops elements with display: none or zero height. Content that only appears after scrolling, in a closed accordion, or in an inactive tab is not collected. Scroll through the page and open what you need before calling preprocess().
  3. Scripts. The body is replaced. <script> elements that were in the body and not inside a slide are gone.

docs.title: A slide is tagged light although it is dark
docs.text:
getBgClass() relies on the colour map. Check these causes:

  • Colour set by other means. Only class rules, an inline background-color, and an existing data-background-color are read. Colours set by an id selector, an element selector, a gradient or an image are not seen, and the slide defaults to slide-light-bg.
  • Named colours. luminance() parses only hex and rgb()/rgba(). Named colours such as navy count as white.
  • Spaces inside rgb() in a <style> element. parseCssBackgroundColors() stops reading a background-color value at the first space. For .x { background-color: rgb(0, 0, 0); } it records rgb(0,, which luminance() cannot parse, so the slide counts as light. Rules from linked stylesheets are read through the CSSOM instead and are not affected, but values from <style> elements override them.
  • Cross-origin stylesheets. Browsers block cssRules access to stylesheets from another origin without CORS headers. Those sheets are skipped silently.

docs.title: stageWidth and stageHeight have no effect
docs.text: They are accepted and given defaults (1920 and 1080) but the current code does not use them. Set the size of the slides in the downstream renderer, and set the browser viewport before calling preprocess(), because the block split measures element positions in the current layout.

docs.title: ReferenceError: document is not defined
docs.text: preprocess() reads the global document and window, and wrapContentsInDiv() (called by normalizeSlideDom()) uses the global Node. In Node.js, run them in a headless browser through page.evaluate() (see Quick start). isChromeElement() and ensureSectionTag() only need Element objects, and the four colour helpers run anywhere.

docs.title: The script tag is blocked
docs.text: A page's Content Security Policy can forbid scripts from a CDN. Use the Chrome extension, which injects the bundle from the extension, or a headless browser with page.addScriptTag().

docs.title: npm install vexy-dexyjs returns 404
docs.text: The package has not been published to npm. Build it from source as described in Installation.
